text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm opening a small Terraform refactor to change how feature flags/configs are wired. Instead of a single global ConfigMap we create per-model ConfigMaps and use an annotation for inheritance fallback. Plan looks straightforward but want quick eyes on secret-sync/labeling implications. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432

maria: Plan snippet (trimmed):
```
# module.model_configs.kubernetes_config_map.per_model["gpt-3.5"] will be created
+ resource "kubernetes_config_map" "per_model" {
  + metadata {
    + name = "flags-gpt-3.5"
    + labels = { "app" = "model-flags", "model" = "gpt-3.5" }
  }
}
# module.global_config.kubernetes_config_map.global_flags will be tainted/removed
```

devin: Can you paste the full diff for the StatefulSet template change? also add the PR link in the changelog.

maria: Full diff (relevant part):
```yaml
- metadata.annotations: {}
+ metadata.annotations: 
+   redwood.com/config-checksum: "${filemd5(\"./manifests/flags-templates/gpt-3.5.yaml\")}"
volumeMounts:
- mountPath: /etc/global/flags
+ mountPath: /etc/models/gpt-3.5/flags
```

ryan: Quick question: our runtime expects flags at /etc/models/<model>/flags with keys prefixed by feature_. Will that mapping still hold for older models?

maria: Yes — the new per-model CM will contain the same keys, we only change the mount path. For any model without a per-model CM we fallback to the global one via annotation logic in the init container.

sasha: Heads-up: secret-syncer currently watches ConfigMaps with label `team=infra` and triggers rollout by adding checksum annotation to Deployments. If we switch labels to `app=model-flags` without keeping `team=infra`, the watcher won't see updates -> no rollout.

maria: Good catch. I can include `team=infra` on the per-model CM resources in TF to preserve the watch. Alternatively we can update secret-syncer selector, but that needs a coordinated change. 

infra-oncall: I can flip secret-syncer to watch `app=model-flags` but prefer to do it in a maintenance window. For safety let's keep the legacy label for 2 release cycles and add a migration plan.

devin: :thumbsup: migration plan should include a one-off job that copies `global-flags` -> per-model CMs for existing models, and a smoke check. Also include a helm values flag to keep legacy label during transition.

maria: I'll add a post-deploy job to the PR: `kubectl get cm global-flags -o jsonpath='{.data}' | kubectl create configmap flags-{{model}} --from-file=-` (pseudo). Will also add a k8s Job manifest to run once after TF apply.

sasha: Left a couple inline comments on the PR re: ordering. Suggested rollout sequence: 1) apply TF (create per-model CMs + keep legacy label), 2) run migration job, 3) bump StatefulSet annotation with checksum, 4) verify smoke tests (health + config file contents).

ryan: Code review ping @devin — can you take a quick look at the checksum templating? worried about unnecessary restarts if checksum calculation uses timestamp.

devin: On it. Quick note — ensure checksum is stable (use filemd5/filehash of template), not `date` or random. Also add unit test for templatefile in our test harness.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll update the PR with: keep `team=infra` label, add migration job, stable checksum, and an entry in RELEASE_NOTES. Waiting for 1 approval then I'll coordinate a release window with infra-oncall. :eyes:

deploy-bot: terraform plan completed for branch refs/pull/432/head — 3 to add, 1 to replace, 0 to destroy. No RBAC changes.

infra-oncall: Once PR is merged ping me and I'll schedule the secret-syncer selector change in the following maintenance window (if needed).

maria: Will do — I'll also add a sentence in the deploy playbook about testing: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /etc/models/<model>/flags | grep feature_` to confirm presence of keys.

ryan: Nice. I think this covers the migration risk. Approving once lint check passes.

maria: Thanks — merging after green CI and one more approve.
